definition: Distinct 311 request ids filed in the 365 days to the run date.
label: observed
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). Counted distinct request ids; the city's CSV repeats about 7% of ids once per caller, so row counts run higher.

definition: Requests filed since 1 Jan 2023 whose status is neither closed nor cancelled.
label: observed
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). Status compared case-insensitively (the file has 'Closed' beside 'CLOSED').

definition: Of the open backlog filed since 2023, those filed more than 365 days before the run date.
label: observed
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). Age measured from the filing time to the latest filing time in the file.

definition: Share of requests carrying the city's own promised completion date (PRJCOMPLETEDATE).
label: observed
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). PRJCOMPLETEDATE is a fixed offset per request type (3 days for a light out, 90 for weeds at a vacant building).

definition: Open requests whose city-set promised date has passed (the Monday list), all years, sensitive codes excluded.
label: observed
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). Open = status neither closed nor cancelled; compared with PRJCOMPLETEDATE at the run date.

definition: Monday-list requests filed in the last 365 days.
label: observed
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID). As n1_open_past_promise, restricted to the last year's filings.

definition: Grass cuts ('Grass Maint' + 'Weed-Grass') per year in the forestry ledger: distinct parcel, date and service type; the raw ledger rows behind them; and the parcels covered.
label: observed
note: Negative result: do not use 2025 ledger figures as evidence of no cut. Use cuts_distinct_parcel_days, not ledger_rows, for any count of cuts (N8 finding 10).
derivation: the Forestry Division's service ledger (forestry-service-records.csv, cuts = 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows). The ledger repeats rows (most pre-2021 legacy rows appear twice), so cuts are counted as distinct parcel, date and type. 2025 is about a third of a normal year; whether cuts went unrecorded or unbilled after the 16 May tornado is not known from the file.

definition: Grass Maint in the forestry ledger in 2026: raw ledger rows; distinct cuts (parcel and date); the parcels they cover; and how many of those are LRA (city land bank) parcels.
label: observed
note: Say 'about 31,500 grass cuts billed on 11,971 parcels', not '37,543 cuts' (37,543 is ledger rows; N8 finding 10).
derivation: the Forestry Division's service ledger (forestry-service-records.csv, cuts = 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows), parcel ids looked up in the LRA inventory (LRA_INVENTORY.csv). The ledger repeats rows, so 'charges' or 'cuts' must be the distinct count, not the row count.

definition: Parcels on the 2026 mowing rotation (at least one Grass Maint cut 1 Apr-30 Sep); median longest gap between consecutive billed cuts; parcels that went more than 42 and more than 90 days without a billed cut (counting the run from the last cut to 30 Sep, so lots cut once count too); parcels cut once; LRA parcels over 90 days; and parcels with more than 90 days strictly between two cuts.
label: observed
note: Say 'went more than 90 days without a billed cut (counting to 30 September)' (N8 finding 15d). The city's rotation runs about eight weeks between cuts, so BUILD-SPEC's 42-day threshold flags almost every lot.
derivation: the Forestry Division's service ledger (forestry-service-records.csv, cuts = 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows), parcel ids looked up in the LRA inventory; a cut is a distinct parcel and date. Posting dates are batched weekly, so gaps are good to about a week.

definition: Inspect City Tree requests cancelled, and cancelled with no public words.
label: observed
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID).

definition: Share of cancelled Inspect City Tree requests whose address appears in the tree removal or trim work-order sample, vs the same share for unrelated requests (residential potholes, refuse, damaged containers).
label: observed
note: Say "appear in Forestry's work orders about five times as often as unrelated requests", not "were converted".
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID) matched by normalised address to Cityworks tree work-order samples (city map server saved searches, 1,500 rows each, staff fields removed). Samples cover 1,500 of 2,522 removals and 1,500 of 6,276 trims, so both shares are lower bounds.

definition: Inspect City Tree requests cancelled with no words, filed more than a day after a Forestry removal order at the same normalised address had started (the order still open in the city's sample); median days the most recent such order had been open; for comparison, the count when any removal order within 30 m is allowed; and all blank-cancelled requests.
label: observed
note: Public text: use the same-address count (N8 conflict 3); within 30 m reaches neighbouring trees. N5 registers 288 / 575 days (n5_tree_cancel_blank_wo_predates, n5_tree_predating_wo_median_age_days) for the same rule; N1's view gives one more request. Framing (COMMON 9): residents report a tree the city already knows must come down; the request is cancelled with no words; the order stays open.
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID) matched by identical normalised address to Cityworks tree work-order samples (city map server saved searches, 1,500 rows each, staff fields removed) (removal orders, saved search 6955); Cityworks dates converted from UTC to Central. Lower bounds: the sample holds 1,500 of 2,522 open removal orders.

definition: Weeds-Vacant Lot requests filed in 2026 on land-bank (LRA) lots, resident-filed, closed within three days as 'on schedule to be cut' or 'added to rotation': requests and lots; and those with no grass cut billed on the lot at any time after filing.
label: observed
note: Public text uses N5's registered 94 requests on 75 lots (n5_funnel_no_cut_requests, n5_funnel_no_cut_lots; N8 conflict 2). N1's wider parcel join (90% vs N5's 83% of 2026 lot requests matched) finds a few more. Requests filed after mid-September have had little time.
derivation: 311 service requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid UTF-8 bytes dropped, one row per REQUESTID) joined by parcel id (through MSD's parcel address file (msd_parcels_stl_city_attrs.jsonl, owner names never read), the LRA inventory and Forestry's maintenance list) to the Forestry Division's service ledger (forestry-service-records.csv, cuts = 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows); LRA ownership from LRA_INVENTORY.csv. N5's rule (COMMON 9). Ledger dates posted in weekly batches; no charge is not proof of no cut.
